43057496.titulo: Antimalarial activity of Croton caudatus Geiseler leaf extract and its ability to reduce experimental cerebral malaria pathogenesis.
43057496.autores: Chatterjee A, Singh N, … Nagaraj VA (7 autores)

resumo_blocos.racional: Embora Croton caudatus Geiseler seja empregado na medicina tradicional contra a malária, faltavam evidências experimentais sobre sua atividade antiplasmódica, seus alvos moleculares no parasito e sua capacidade de conter a patogênese da malária cerebral experimental (ECM).
resumo_blocos.metodologia: O extrato metanólico foliar (CcLE) foi fracionado em frações aquosa (CcWater), butanólica (CcBut), clorofórmica (CcChl) e hexânica (CcHex). Avaliaram-se atividade antiplasmódica in vitro contra Plasmodium falciparum (cepas Pf3D7 e PfCam3.IR539T), citotoxicidade, hemólise, perfilamento químico da fração mais ativa, inibição da polimerização de β-hematina, quantificação de hemozoína e dosagem de espécies reativas de oxigênio (ROS). Testaram-se ainda toxicidade oral aguda e supressão parasitária em camundongos BALB/c com Plasmodium berghei ANKA (PbA), integridade da barreira hematoencefálica, expressão de citocinas/quimiocinas e infiltrado imune cerebral em camundongos C57BL/6 com ECM, além de gametocitemia e exflagelação ex vivo.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A fração CcHex apresentou a maior potência contra Pf3D7 (IC50 = 6,84 ± 0,61 μg/mL) sem citotoxicidade nem hemólise detectáveis e com perfil seguro em toxicidade aguda. CcHex inibiu a formação de β-hematina em ensaio livre de células, reduziu hemozoína em Pf3D7, elevou ROS intracelulares no parasito e comprometeu a formação de gametócitos e a exflagelação masculina. In vivo, produziu ~62% de supressão parasitária em BALB/c a 1000 mg/kg/dia e protegeu C57BL/6 da ECM ao preservar a barreira hematoencefálica e reduzir TNF-α, IFN-γ, CXCL9, CXCL10, CXCR3, ICAM-1 e infiltração cerebral de linfócitos T CD8+.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Dialoga diretamente com o modelo murino PbA/C57BL/6J do LUCHM ao conectar a inibição da detoxificação de hemo e o estresse oxidativo parasitário à preservação da barreira hematoencefálica e à atenuação do recrutamento de células T CD8+ via CXCL9/CXCL10/CXCR3 e ICAM-1.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Malária Cerebral & Neuroinflamação' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Avaliar no modelo PbA/C57BL/6J do LUCHM se moléculas que bloqueiam a polimerização de β-hematina protegem as junções oclusivas (claudina-5 e ZO-1) indiretamente pela redução da carga microvascular ou por ação endotelial direta.

43057496.resumo:
Croton caudatus Geiseler is widely used in traditional medicine to treat various ailments, including malaria. However, scientific evidences supporting its antimalarial activity and the associated molecular mechanisms, and its potential to reduce severe malaria complications are lacking.
The present study was aimed to evaluate the antimalarial activity of C. caudatus leaf extract and its fractions, and to investigate the underlying molecular mechanisms.
Methanolic leaf extract of C. caudatus (CcLE) was fractionated into water (CcWater), butanol (CcBut), chloroform (CcChl), and hexane (CcHex) fractions. In vitro antiplasmodial activity was assessed against two different strains of Plasmodium falciparum (Pf): Pf3D7 and PfCam3.IR539T, alongside cytotoxicity and hemolysis assays. Phytochemical profiling of the most active fraction was performed by chemical fingerprinting. Mechanistic studies included β-hematin polymerization inhibition, hemozoin quantification, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) measurement. Acute oral toxicity and in vivo antimalarial efficacy were carried out in Plasmodium berghei (Pb) ANKA-infected BALB/c mice. Experimental cerebral malaria (ECM) studies were performed in Pb ANKA-infected C57BL/6 mice through the assessment of blood-brain barrier integrity, inflammatory marker expression, and immune cell infiltration analyses. Examining the gametocyte numbers and ex vivo exflagellation assays were carried out with Pb ANKA-infected mouse blood to assess the gametocytocidal activity.
CcHex exhibited the highest antiplasmodial activity against Pf 3D7 (IC50 = 6.84 ± 0.61 μg/mL) without detectable cytotoxic or hemolytic effects. Phytochemical analysis suggested the presence of bioactive metabolites associated with antimalarial activity. CcHex inhibited β-hematin formation in a cell-free assay and reduced hemozoin levels in Pf3D7 parasites, supporting its potential to interfere with parasite heme detoxification. It also increased intracellular ROS levels in the parasites, suggesting the disruption of heme detoxification. Further, CcHex treatment reduced gametocyte formation and impaired male gametocyte exflagellation, indicating gametocytocidal activity. Acute toxicity studies demonstrated a favourable safety profile. In Pb-infected Balb/c mice, CcHex treatment produced ∼62% parasite suppression at 1000 mg/kg/day. Importantly, CcHex treatment could protect against ECM by preserving blood-brain barrier integrity, and significantly reducing the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α and IFN-γ), chemokines (CXCL9, CXCL10, and CXCR3), the adhesion molecule ICAM-1, and CD8+ T-cell infiltration in the brain.
The present study demonstrates that C. caudatus, a traditionally used medicinal plant, possesses significant antiplasmodial activity, exhibits protective effects against ECM, and impairs male gametocyte exflagellation. CcHex showed potent antimalarial efficacy through inhibition of parasite heme detoxification, induction of oxidative stress, and modulation of host inflammatory responses. These results support the ethnopharmacological use of C. caudatus and highlight its potential as a source of bioactive phytochemicals for the development of novel antimalarials and adjunctive therapies against severe malaria.

43057892.titulo: The Indian Jumping Ant Harpegnathos saltator as a Model to Study Brain Plasticity and Epigenetics.
43057892.autores: Moreno-Medina S, Kuang M, … Khan S (5 autores)

resumo_blocos.racional: A regulação epigenética sustenta a plasticidade neural frente a estímulos ambientais e sociais, mas modelos vertebrados raramente exibem reversibilidade fenotípica completa na vida adulta. Na formiga saltadora indiana Harpegnathos saltator, operárias adultas convertem-se reversivelmente em reprodutoras (gamergates), porém faltavam protocolos consolidados que assegurassem reprodutibilidade entre laboratórios.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Os autores apresentam uma síntese metodológica e conceitual do sistema Harpegnathos saltator, descrevendo o protocolo conceitual da transição operária-gamergate e compilando os recursos genômicos e epigenômicos desenvolvidos para investigar expressão gênica, sinalização endócrina, neuropeptídeos e composição celular do cérebro durante essa plasticidade adulta.
resumo_blocos.resultados: O trabalho detalha como a transição socialmente induzida e reversível entre operária e gamergate coordena alterações comportamentais, fisiológicas e neurais, envolvendo variações em neuropeptídeos, regulação epigenética e rearranjo da composição celular cerebral. Ao consolidar os recursos moleculares existentes, estabelece um roteiro para padronização experimental dessa espécie como modelo de neuroepigenética.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Apesar de focado em formiga eussocial e não em culicídeos, oferece referências técnicas de genômica funcional, epigenômica e dinâmica de neuropeptídeos cerebrais aplicáveis ao eixo neuroendócrino que governa comportamento alimentar e reprodutivo em insetos vetores no LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Neurobiologia, Neuropeptídeos & Eixo Intestino-Cérebro' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Comparar famílias de neuropeptídeos e marcadores de remodelamento epigenético descritos na transição reprodutiva de H. saltator com vias neuroendócrinas ativadas pós-repasto sanguíneo em fêmeas de Aedes aegypti.

43057892.resumo: Epigenetic regulation of gene expression plays a central role in brain plasticity during development and adulthood, and in response to the environment. While vertebrate models have provided important insights into these processes, systems that exhibit inducible and reversible plasticity throughout adulthood offer unique opportunities to investigate how environmental and social cues drive long-lasting changes in the brain, behavior, and physiology. Eusocial insects are well suited for such studies because individuals sharing nearly identical genomes can develop distinct behavioral, physiological, and reproductive phenotypes through socially regulated molecular, endocrine, and epigenetic pathways. The Indian jumping ant, Harpegnathos saltator, is of particular interest because adult workers can reversibly transition into a queen-like reproductive state called the gamergate. This transition involves coordinated behavioral, physiological, and neural changes, including alterations in gene expression, neuropeptide levels, and brain cellular composition. Despite the growing number of research groups using Harpegnathos, standardized and systematic protocols for working with these insects are lacking. Here, we provide a general overview of Harpegnathos, describe the worker-gamergate transition, and discuss its utility for studying brain plasticity and neuroepigenetic regulation. We further summarize the genomic and epigenomic resources that have been developed to date for the molecular characterization of brain plasticity in this species, and highlight the need for a consolidated set of standardized protocols to support reproducible research using Harpegnathos Such approaches will lower technical barriers to working with Harpegnathos and further establish it as a powerful model for linking social behavior, brain plasticity, and genome regulation.

43061583.titulo: A Standardized Rearing Procedure for Aedes aegypti (Diptera: Culicidae): Implications for Laboratory-Based Vector Competence and Control Studies.
43061583.autores: Asgarian TS, Moosa-Kazemi SH, … Sedaghat MM (5 autores)

resumo_blocos.racional: A confiabilidade dos ensaios de competência vetorial e controle de Aedes aegypti depende de colônias de insetário padronizadas, mas variações no tempo de secagem dos papéis de ovos e nos meios de estímulo à eclosão geram oscilações acentuadas na viabilidade larval.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Em insetário controlado em Bandar Abbas (Irã), parâmetros ambientais foram monitorados continuamente durante a criação larval sob dieta programada e manutenção de adultos com solução de sacarose e repasto sanguíneo. Avaliaram-se a correlação entre a duração da secagem do papel de postura e a porcentagem de eclosão, além da comparação da taxa de eclosão em três meios: água fervida resfriada, levedura e ração larval.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Detectou-se forte correlação negativa entre o tempo de secagem dos papéis de ovos e a taxa de eclosão (Pearson r = -0,818; p < 0,001), com a secagem gradual por dois dias atingindo mais de 90% de eclosão sem necessidade de estimulantes. Não houve diferença significativa entre os três meios de eclosão testados (F = 0,601; p = 0,578), e observou-se que 20% a 30% dos ovos foram depositados diretamente sobre a superfície da água nas ovitrampas.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Oferece parâmetros operacionais imediatos para o insetário de Aedes aegypti do LUCHM, validando a secagem gradual de dois dias para eclosão acima de 90% e alertando para a postura direta na água ao quantificar fecundidade em fêmeas submetidas a diferentes dietas.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Quantificar no insetário do LUCHM se fêmeas alimentadas com sangue de camundongos em dieta HFHS alteram a proporção de oviposição direta na água em comparação à postura em papel-filtro.

43061583.resumo:
Aedes aegypti is a major vector of numerous arboviruses, including dengue, Zika, chikungunya and yellow fever. This study aimed to establish a standardized and practical procedure for maintaining and propagating an Ae. aegypti colony under controlled insectary conditions in Bandar Abbas, Iran.
Environmental parameters were routinely monitored. Larvae were reared with an appropriate diet under a regular feeding schedule, while adult mosquitoes were provided with a sucrose solution and blood meals. The correlation between the duration of egg paper drying and the hatching percentage was evaluated. Hatching rates were compared across three media: cooled boiled water, yeast and larval food.
A strong negative correlation was observed between drying duration and hatching percentage, with a Pearson correlation of -0.818 (p< 0.001). Gradual drying of egg papers over a period of two days resulted in a hatching rate of over 90% without any hatching stimulant. No significant differences in hatching rates were found among the three media, as indicated by F= 0.601 (p= 0.578). In a novel observation, female mosquitoes were found to deposit approximately 20-30% of their eggs directly on the water surface inside ovitraps under insectary conditions in Iran.
This study provides a reliable, low-cost model for rearing Ae. aegypti in research insectaries and facilitates future studies on vector control.

43058765.titulo: Provenance and competence for CHIKV and DENV of Aedes albopictus populations.
43058765.autores: Piccinno R, Madec Y, … Malacrida AR (11 autores)

resumo_blocos.racional: A invasão de Aedes albopictus na bacia do Mediterrâneo desde os anos 1980 envolveu múltiplas introduções descontínuas e mistura genômica entre linhagens. O estudo investigou se essa heterogeneidade de ancestralidade genética explica variações locais na competência vetorial para os vírus Chikungunya (CHIKV), Dengue (DENV) e Zika (ZIKV).
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Populações de Ae. albopictus de referência ancestral (Guangzhou, China) e de dez localidades adventícias em cinco regiões mediterrâneas (Sul da Suíça, Norte e Centro da Itália, Bálcãs e Grécia) foram genotipadas por marcadores microssatélites (SSR), inferindo-se ancestralidade e demografia via STRUCTURE (v2.3.2.0) e DIYABC-RF. A competência vetorial para CHIKV (06.21), DENV-1 e ZIKV (PE243) foi avaliada por taxas de infecção, eficiência de disseminação e eficiência de transmissão em modelos univariados e multivariados.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A reconstrução demográfica revelou colonização mediterrânea caótica e descontínua com intensa mistura gênica, gerando acentuado mosaico espacial de ancestralidade. Essa heterogeneidade genética modulou significativamente a competência vetorial sobretudo para CHIKV e DENV: populações geograficamente próximas com ancestralidades distintas diferiram fortemente em competência, enquanto populações distantes de ancestralidade compartilhada exibiram perfis semelhantes para CHIKV e DENV.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Ressalta para os estudos de imunidade antiviral e competência vetorial no LUCHM que o histórico genético e o grau de mistura das populações de Aedes condicionam as barreiras de infecção e disseminação para arbovírus como DENV-1 e CHIKV.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Associar o perfil de competência para DENV e CHIKV em linhagens brasileiras de Aedes a marcadores genéticos populacionais e à eficiência de resposta antiviral mediada por RNAi no intestino médio.

43058765.resumo:
Aedes albopictus is one of the world's most hazardous invasive species, increasingly implicated in the autochthonous transmission of Chikungunya (CHIKV) and Dengue (DENV) viruses in newly colonized areas. Since invading the Mediterranean Basin several in the early 1980s, recurrent introductions of distinct lineages have driven extensive genomic admixture within adventive populations. This study investigates whether and how the complex dynamics of these diverse genetic backgrounds have shaped variations in vector competence for CHIKV, DENV, and Zika (ZIKV) viruses.
Using highly polymorphic simple sequence repeat (SSR) markers, we genotyped Ae. Albopictus samples from an ancestral population (Guangzhou, China) and ten adventive populations across five Mediterranean regions (Southern Switzerland, Northern/Central Italy, the Balkans, and Greece). Genetic ancestry and demographic histories were inferred using Bayesian STRUCTURE (v2.3.2.0) and DIYABC-RF. The association between population ancestry and vector competence for CHIKV (06.21), DENV-1, and ZIKV (PE243) was assessed using infection rate, dissemination efficiency, and transmission efficiency indices, analyzed via univariate and multivariate models.
Combining historical records with demographic models revealed that the establishment of Ae. Albopictus in the Mediterranean was driven by chaotic, discontinuous lineage introductions and admixture events, resulting in high spatial and ancestry heterogeneity. Notably, this genetic heterogeneity significantly influences vector competence, in particular for CHIKV and DENV. Interestingly, populations in neighboring geographical areas with distinct ancestries exhibited drastically different competence profiles, whereas geographically distant populations sharing genetic ancestry displayed similar vector competence for CHIKV and DENV.
Our findings demonstrate that the complex population dynamics and colonization history of Ae. Albopictus contributes to variation in vector competence, altering the geographical landscape of arboviral risk. These results underscore the urgent need for localized, geographically tailored vector control strategies in Europe, a region facing a rising trend of both imported and autochthonous arboviral infections.

43058170.titulo: MitoEM 2.0: A Benchmark for Challenging 3D Mitochondria Instance Segmentation from EM Images.
43058170.autores: Liu P, Shen B, … Wei D (9 autores)

resumo_blocos.racional: Algoritmos de segmentação de instâncias mitocondriais em 3D por microscopia eletrônica de volume (vEM) perdem acurácia em cenários ultracompactos, redes hiperfusionadas e conexões filamentosas delgadas de contorno ambíguo devido à falta de benchmarks multiescala padronizados.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: O MitoEM 2.0 estende o benchmark MitoEM reunindo volumes multiescala de vEM adquiridos por FIB-SEM, SBF-SEM e ssSEM em diferentes tecidos e espécies, com segmentação de instâncias verificada por especialistas e submetida a controle de qualidade e reindexação. Os dados são disponibilizados em resoluções nativas e processadas, nos formatos NIfTI (compatível com nnU-Net) e OME-Zarr para fluxos em nuvem, acompanhados de metadados por volume (tamanho de voxel, modalidade, tecido, partições oficiais de treino/validação/teste), somas de verificação e scripts de linha de base.
resumo_blocos.resultados: O conjunto consolidado oferece volumes anotados especificamente calibrados para situações biologicamente difíceis — empacotamento mitocondrial denso, redes fusionadas e túbulos finos — com partições reproduzíveis e métricas estratificadas por tamanho que permitem treinamento robusto e comparação justa entre métodos de segmentação 3D.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Recurso técnico de alto valor imediato para a frente de Microscopia Eletrônica de Volume no CENABIO/UFRJ (FIB-SEM e SBF-SEM), acelerando pipelines de segmentação mitocondrial em NIfTI/nnU-Net e OME-Zarr para reconstruções 3D de protozoários e células de vetores.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Microscopia Eletrônica de Volume & Bioimagem' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Treinar ou calibrar modelos nnU-Net a partir dos pesos e partições do MitoEM 2.0 sobre tomogramas FIB-SEM do CENABIO para segmentar mitocôndrias e mapear sítios de contato com acidocalcisomos e gotas lipídicas.

43058170.resumo: We present MitoEM 2.0, a difficulty-aware extension of the original MitoEM benchmark for training and evaluating three-dimensional (3D) mitochondria instance segmentation in volume electron microscopy. The collection assembles multiscale vEM datasets (FIB-SEM, SBF-SEM, ssSEM) spanning diverse tissues and species, with expert-verified instance labels emphasizing biologically difficult scenarios, including dense mitochondrial packing, hyperfused networks, and thin filamentous connections with ambiguous boundaries. All releases include native-resolution volumes and standardized processed versions, per-volume metadata (voxel size, modality, tissue, splits), and official train/validation/test partitions to enable reproducible benchmarking. Annotations follow a consistent protocol with quality checks and instance reindexing. Data are provided in NIfTI with nnU-Net-compatible layout and OME-Zarr for cloud-aware workflows, alongside machine-readable split files and checksums. Baseline scripts support common training pipelines and size-stratified evaluation. By consolidating challenging volumes and harmonized labels, MitoEM 2.0 facilitates robust model development and fair comparison across methods while supporting reuse in bioimage analysis, algorithm benchmarking, and teaching.

43061087.titulo: Insecticide Resistance Dynamics in Aedes aegypti (Diptera: Culicidae) from Different Habitats in the Punjab, Pakistan.
43061087.autores: Hayat M, Nasir S, … Sultana S (4 autores)

resumo_blocos.racional: O emprego intensivo de inseticidas químicos contra Aedes aegypti tem selecionado rapidamente resistência múltipla, tornando essencial monitorar o perfil de susceptibilidade em populações de campo frente a diferentes classes químicas, larvicidas bacterianos e enzimas detoxificantes.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Durante 2024–2025 no Punjab (Paquistão), três linhagens de campo de Ae. aegypti provenientes de áreas com histórico de controle químico foram comparadas à linhagem suscetível de laboratório (LAB) e à linhagem Tidiwala (TDW) de área rural sem ou com mínimo uso de inseticidas. The mosquito Aedes aegypti is the most important vector of many viral diseases, such as dengue virus. Thus, various chemical insecticides are being used to control this vector. On the other hand, due to the intensive blind use of chemical insecticides, mosquito vectors are rapidly developing resistance against most of them.
The present study was conducted during 2024-25 to explore the development of resistance in three Ae. aegypti strains with a previous history of insecticidal records compared with Laboratory (LAB) and Tidiwala (TDW) strains collected from localities (Tidiwala and rural barren land) with no or minimal use of insecticides. Resistance development was recorded by utilizing five commonly used insecticides against mosquitoes in Punjab, Pakistan.
Results showed that deltamethrin was the best during 2024 when compared with alpha-cypermethrin, temephos, lambda-cyhalothrin and Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis. All field-collected strains revealed significant resistance to the tested insecticides compared with LAB and TDW strains. The same findings were reflected in the enzyme spectrum (glutathione-S-transferase, mixed-function oxidases, esterase, and acetylcholinesterase).
These results may help to devise a comprehensive future strategy for mosquito control through selective insecticides by limiting the spread of resistance.

43061110.titulo: Challenges and Opportunities for Integrated Vector Management in Developing Countries: A Narrative Review with a Focus on Iran.
43061110.autores: Dehghan O, Ghaffari J, … Azarm A (8 autores)

resumo_blocos.racional: Doenças transmitidas por artrópodes vetores mantêm alta carga em países em desenvolvimento diante de urbanização e mudanças ambientais. Embora o Manejo Integrado de Vetores (IVM) proposto pela OMS articule controle baseado em evidências, vigilância e participação comunitária, sua execução permanece fragmentada em cenários de recursos limitados.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Revisão narrativa abrangendo literatura indexada em PubMed, Scopus e Web of Science, documentos técnicos da OMS e relatórios regionais de vigilância publicados entre 2000 e 2025, examinando barreiras operacionais, princípios de IVM e oportunidades de política pública com foco no Irã.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Identificaram-se gargalos interligados na implementação do IVM: financiamento instável, fraca articulação intersetorial, falhas na vigilância entomológica e epidemiológica, baixa adesão comunitária, carência de capacitação técnica e expansão da resistência a inseticidas. 43061110.resumo:
Vector-borne diseases (VBDs), caused by pathogens transmitted through the bites of infected arthropod vectors, remain a major public health challenge in many developing countries. Environmental changes, urbanization, population mobility and health system limitations continue to sustain the transmission of these pathogens and the diseases they cause. Integrated Vector Management (IVM), recommended by the World Health Organization, provides a sustainable framework that combines evidence-based vector control interventions with surveillance, intersectoral collaboration, and community participation. However, implementation of IVM remains inconsistent, particularly in resource-limited settings.
This narrative review synthesized evidence from peer-reviewed literature indexed in PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science, supplemented by WHO technical guidance documents and regional surveillance reports published between 2000 and 2025. The review focused on IVM principles, implementation barriers, operational challenges and policy opportunities, with particular emphasis on Iran.
The review identified several interconnected barriers limiting effective IVM implementation, including unstable financing, insufficient intersectoral coordination, gaps in entomological and epidemiological surveillance, limited community participation, inadequate technical capacity and increasing insecticide resistance. Evidence from Iran demonstrates substantial progress in malaria control while highlighting ongoing challenges related to leishmaniasis, emerging Aedes-borne disease risks, resistance management, and the need for stronger integration of environmental and surveillance systems.
Achieving sustainable reductions in VBD burden will depend on long-term commitment to integrated governance, resistance-informed decision-making and context-specific strategies that enable countries such as Iran and other developing settings to build resilient vector control systems.

43061626.titulo: Laboratory Evaluation of a Non-Insecticide Multimodal Trap Using Carbon Dioxide, Lactic Acid, Ultraviolet-A Light and Sound Frequency for Aedes aegypti Control.

resumo_blocos.racional: Como o uso repetido de inseticidas químicos contra Aedes aegypti promove resistência e contaminação ambiental, cresce a demanda por armadilhas físicas não inseticidas que combinem múltiplos estímulos atrativos para captura eficiente no ambiente doméstico.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Estudo quase-experimental em laboratório avaliando um protótipo de armadilha multimodal não inseticida que integra dióxido de carbono (CO2), ácido láctico, luz ultravioleta-A (UV-A) e frequência sonora. Utilizaram-se 2.850 fêmeas de Ae. aegypti não alimentadas com sangue (3 a 5 dias de vida, colônia da Universitas Gadjah Mada, Yogyakarta, Indonésia), em triplicatas de 50 mosquitos por tratamento, comparando combinações de atrativos e o protótipo em sala fechada frente à armadilha Mosquito Killer BG-360, à Photocatalyst Mosquito and Fly Trap e a controle negativo apenas de sucção, analisados por Modelo Linear Geral e ANOVA de medidas repetidas.

43061626.resumo:
Dengue remains an important public health problem in tropical and subtropical settings. Aedes aegypti is a principal dengue vector and is highly adapted to domestic environments. Because repeated chemical-based control may contribute to insecticide resistance and environmental exposure, practical non-insecticide tools are needed. This study evaluated a non-insecticide multimodal trap integrating carbon dioxide, lactic acid, ultraviolet-A light and sound frequency for Ae. aegypti control.
This quasi-experimental study evaluated a laboratory prototype multimodal trap. A total of 2,850 female Ae. aegypti mosquitoes were used for multimodal combination testing and commercial-trap comparison after preliminary attractant optimization. The colony was obtained from the Parasitology Laboratory, Faculty of Medicine, Public Health and Nursing, Universitas Gadjah Mada, Yogyakarta, Indonesia. Non-blood-fed females aged 3-5 days were used. Each treatment included three replications of 50 mosquitoes. Outcomes were analyzed using the General Linear Model and repeated ANOVA.
Lactic acid was the most effective single attractant (78.66%). The four-mode combination produced the highest mean effectiveness (91.33%), with a maximum observed value of 98%. In the enclosed-room test, the multimodal trap performed significantly better than the Mosquito Killer BG-360 and the suction-only negative control, but not significantly better than the Photocatalyst Mosquito and Fly Trap.
The non-insecticide multimodal trap showed promising laboratory effectiveness for capturing or electrocuting Ae. aegypti. Semi-field and field trials are needed to assess operational effectiveness, feasibility, electrical safety and durability.

43057552.titulo: Entomological survey for potential Anopheles malaria vectors and their insecticide resistance status in agricultural and peri-urban sites of Central and Southern Greece.
43057552.autores: Balaska S, Parnassa V, … Kioulos I (10 autores)

resumo_blocos.racional: Embora a Grécia tenha eliminado a malária há décadas, mudanças climáticas e fluxos populacionais mantêm risco de reintrodução, exigindo dados atualizados sobre a presença de espécies competentes de Anopheles, seu perfil de resistência a inseticidas e eventual infecção parasitária.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Coletas entomológicas em áreas agrícolas e periurbanas da Grécia central e meridional entre 2021 e 2024 foram identificadas por código de barras de DNA multilocus. Subamostras passaram por bioensaios de resistência a inseticidas segundo diretrizes do CDC e bioensaios larvais da OMS para Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis (Bti), genotipagem de mutações no gene do canal de sódio dependente de voltagem (alelo L1014) e pesquisa molecular de Plasmodium em fêmeas adultas de Phthiotis.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Identificaram-se cinco espécies de Anopheles, incluindo vetores competentes de malária como An. sacharovi, An. labranchiae e An. claviger. Os bioensaios detectaram resistência à deltametrina na Coríntia e Beócia e possível resistência em Phthiotis, enquanto todas as populações testadas tenderam à susceptibilidade frente ao larvicida Bti; o sequenciamento revelou apenas o alelo selvagem L1014 no canal de sódio, e todos os adultos de Phthiotis testaram negativos para Plasmodium.

resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Rastrear em colônias resistentes a piretróides sem mutação L1014 quais enzimas metabólicas ou barreiras cuticulares sustentam o fenótipo de resistência antes da perda de eficácia de Bti.

43057552.resumo: Greece has eliminated malaria for several decades now, however the ecological settings as being transformed in response to climatic crisis and the current geo-political situation may pose an epidemiological risk. Evidence on Anopheles vector species occurrence and their insecticide resistance (IR) profile in the country is limited and this study aims to narrow this gap. To this end, Anopheles collections were performed in selected agricultural and peri-urban sites throughout Greece, during 2021-2024. Α sub-set of the populations was assessed for their response to insecticides commonly used in the country, showing evidence of resistance to deltamethrin in Corinthia and Boeotia, and possible resistance for the Phthiotis collection, based on CDC guidelines, while all the characterized populations showed a tendency towards susceptibility to the bacterial larvicide Bti (WHO larval bioassays). A multi-locus DNA barcoding approach identified totally five Anopheles species, with distinct abundances and distribution patterns, including epidemiologically relevant malaria vectors, such as An. sacharovi, Αn. labranchiae and An. claviger. In parallel, monitoring of common pyrethroid resistance-associated mutations in the voltage-gated sodium channel gene revealed the exclusive presence of the wild-type allele L1014. Lastly, a Plasmodium parasite detection assay was applied in the adult Anopheles specimens from Phthiotis producing negative results. In all, our survey updates the Anopheles species distribution map of central and southern Greece and provides valuable evidence on populations' IR status, to support future vector control targeted initiatives. The presence of malaria competent vector species, along with sporadic deltamethrin resistance records, stress the importance of systematic monitoring practices to maintain malaria transmission elimination.

43061606.resumo:
Aedes albopictus, a key vector of arboviral diseases, has already been detected in Guilan Province, Iran, and is emerging as a public health concern in the country. This study aimed to identify monthly high-risk areas of Ae. albopictus and predict its distribution in Guilan Province using ecological niche modeling under current and projected climate scenarios. Guilan Province, with its high annual influx of travellers and active maritime ports, represents a strategic area for monitoring Ae. albopictus establishment.
A total of 200 occurrence points were obtained from local entomological surveys and health authorities. Four MaxEnt models were developed: current baseline (bioclimatic variables + elevation); current enhanced (bioclimatic variables + elevation + LST, NDVI, NDWI and population); and two future scenarios (SSP1-2.6 and SSP5-8.5, year 2030, CMIP6). Model performance was excellent, with AUC values of 0.909 and 0.908 for the baseline and enhanced models, respectively. Monthly thermal suitability maps were generated based on 2024 meteorological data using the optimal temperature range of 15-35 °C.
Under the SSP5-8.5 scenario, risk areas expanded, and the monthly analysis indicated that nearly the entire Guilan Province exhibited suitable conditions for seven months of the year. The warm months showed the highest probability of Ae. albopictus presence across the province.
These findings provide critical insights for targeted vector surveillance and control strategies in the region.

43058501.titulo: Early detection of dengue outbreaks from routine primary health care records: evaluation by an extended version of the Mixed Model of Artificial Intelligence and Next-Generation (MMAING).
43058501.autores: Borges DGF, Coutinho ER, … Andrade RFS (13 autores)

resumo_blocos.racional: A recently proposed surveillance framework is used to detect arbovirus outbreaks. It mixes traditional compartmental models with artificial intelligence techniques applied to large volumes of unconventional data on syndromic events, environment, and social information, and its performance is evaluated in the early identification of dengue epidemic events in Brazil at municipal level.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: It mixes traditional compartmental models with artificial intelligence techniques applied to large volumes of unconventional data on syndromic events, environment, and social information, and its performance is evaluated in the early identification of dengue epidemic events in Brazil at municipal level. We evaluated an extended version of the MMAING model, referred to as MMAING-Arbo, developed to enable the early detection of dengue outbreaks based on primary health care (PHC) encounters associated with specific arboviral syndromes at the municipal level in Brazil.

The comparative evaluation with EARS demonstrated that MMAING-Arbo performs comparably to or outperforms the EARS variants (C1, C2, and C3) across different epidemiological contexts, with performances varying according to municipal population size.

A recently proposed surveillance framework is used to detect arbovirus outbreaks. It mixes traditional compartmental models with artificial intelligence techniques applied to large volumes of unconventional data on syndromic events, environment, and social information, and its performance is evaluated in the early identification of dengue epidemic events in Brazil at municipal level.
We evaluated an extended version of the MMAING model, referred to as MMAING-Arbo, developed to enable the early detection of dengue outbreaks based on primary health care (PHC) encounters associated with specific arboviral syndromes at the municipal level in Brazil. The analysis covered the period from January 1, 2023, to July 1, 2024, encompassing 2,767 municipalities (49.68% of all municipalities in the country) and identifying a total of 3,478 epidemic events of varying duration observed in the PHC data.

In particular, MMAING-Arbo showed a lower alarm burden per outbreak in larger municipalities, while the EARS-C2 variant achieved higher sensitivity and timeliness in smaller ones.
The analysis of PHC data for multiple mosquito-borne diseases using MMAING-Arbo yields promising results and indicates it might be a valuable tool to issue EWS of emerging outbreaks in real-life conditions. These findings reinforce the importance that future surveillance systems include data-driven approaches that benefit from the integration of multiple models, strengthening sensitivity, specificity, and timeliness of EWS.

43059912.titulo: Evolutionarily distinct dengue virus type 2 with a unique type-specific neutralization determinant.
43059912.autores: Mayer SV, Winkelmann ER, … Katzelnick LC (16 autores)
43059912.revista: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

resumo_blocos.racional: Linhagens silvestres divergentes do vírus da Dengue posicionadas entre os quatro sorotipos canônicos na filogenia levantam a questão de quanto diferenças genotípicas implicam escape antigênico frente à neutralização sorotípica clássica.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Os autores caracterizaram antigenicamente a cepa divergente QML-22 de Bornéu (próxima a DENV-2) por cartografia antigênica, ensaios de neutralização com soros humanos endêmicos de DENV1–4, anticorpo monoclonal potente anti-DENV-2 (3F9) dirigido ao domínio I da proteína de envelope (E), depleção heteróloga de antissoros de primatas não humanos infectados com QML-22 ou com a cepa de referência DENV-2 S16803 e análises evolutivas de pressão seletiva sobre epítopos neutralizantes.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Embora QML-22 tenha se agrupado com cepas globais de DENV-2 no mapa antigênico, foi menos neutralizada por soros contra DENV-2 endêmico e melhor neutralizada por soros de DENV-1, 3 e 4 do que outras cepas DENV-2. QML-22 exibiu um agrupamento de resíduos distintos no domínio I da proteína E que reduziu em >1000 vezes a neutralização pelo anticorpo 3F9, cujo epítopo mostrou pressão seletiva relaxada na análise evolutiva; ensaios de depleção heteróloga confirmaram que a neutralização homóloga depende de epítopos distintos.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Relevante para a vigilância de diversidade antigênica de flavivírus e ensaios com arbovírus em Aedes, mostrando que mutações concentradas no domínio I da proteína E podem gerar escape acentuado a anticorpos neutralizantes específicos mesmo dentro do agrupamento DENV-2.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Verificar se variantes de domínio I da proteína E com perfil antigênico intermediário mantêm eficiência de ligação e entrada no intestino médio de Aedes aegypti.

43059912.resumo:
Dengue viruses 1-4 (DENV1-4) mostly circulate in endemic cycles involving humans and Aedes mosquitoes. However, rare dengue outbreaks originate from non-human primates. These spillovers are caused by sylvatic virus genotypes that are closely related to endemic strains of the same serotype, but some are caused by strains that fall between the four canonical serotypes on phylogenetic trees. It is not clear whether these genotypic differences are reflected in corresponding antigenic differences. Here, we characterized the antigenic features of QML-22, a divergent strain most closely related to DENV2. On an antigenic map, QML-22 clustered with other globally representative DENV2 strains. QML-22 was not as well neutralized by antisera raised against endemic DENV2 and was better neutralized by antisera from DENV1, 3, and 4 infections than other strains of DENV2. QML-22 had a cluster of distinct amino acid residues in domain I of the envelope (E) protein, with only scattered point mutations elsewhere in the envelope. A potently neutralizing anti-DENV2 antibody that targets this site in domain I of the E protein, 3F9, had >1000-fold lower neutralization of QML-22 than other endemic DENV2 strains, whereas other cross-reactive and DENV2-specific antibodies neutralized QML-22 and endemic strains to similar titers. When antisera from non-human primates infected with QML-22 or DENV2 reference strain S16803 were depleted with the heterologous virions, homologous neutralization was unaffected but heterologous neutralization was reduced, suggesting homologous neutralization was due to distinct epitopes. Evolutionary analyses showed the 3F9 epitope was under relaxed selection pressure compared to other neutralizing epitopes and that QML-22 had unique amino acids in this epitope relative to the likely common ancestor of all DENV2. These findings provide insight into the antigenic diversification of DENV and the possible evolution of new serotypes.
Dengue viruses that are most distantly related to the four canonical serotypes originated in Borneo, suggesting this island is a possible site of early dengue virus diversification as well as continued evolution within an unidentified host species. Here, we find divergent strain QML-22 from Borneo shares many neutralizing epitopes with DENV2 but has a distinct epitope in an important region affecting potent DENV2 neutralization. This region of the virus also is variable within DENV2 and in other DENV serotypes, highlighting an important site of dengue virus diversification and evolution. The spillover threat of viruses like QML-22 remains unknown, but ecological changes in Borneo may increase this risk.

43057217.titulo: Zoonotic Malaria Beyond Elimination: Making One Health Accountable.
43057217.revista: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH

resumo_blocos.racional: A malária zoonótica causada por Plasmodium knowlesi, hoje principal causa de malária na Malásia, evidencia que interromper a transmissão humano-humano não basta para eliminar a doença, enquanto o arcabouço de Saúde Única (One Health) carece frequentemente de critérios objetivos para priorizar recursos entre intervenções.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Artigo de análise crítica e proposição estratégica que examina a alocação de esforços em vigilância epidemiológica, ecologia de reservatórios silvestres, manejo clínico e políticas de Saúde Única aplicadas à malária zoonótica por P. knowlesi.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Os autores argumentam que ações contra malária zoonótica devem ser hierarquizadas conforme as decisões concretas que orientam e seu potencial direto de reduzir morbidade e mortalidade. A prontidão clínica — reconhecimento precoce, encaminhamento ágil e tratamento da malária grave — deve permanecer como prioridade máxima por ser a única medida atualmente associada a melhores desfechos clínicos, devendo estudos ecológicos e de fauna ser julgados pela capacidade de gerar respostas acionáveis.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Contextualiza os limites operacionais do controle vetorial e de reservatórios em ciclos zoonóticos de Plasmodium, reforçando a necessidade de distinguir ações ecológicas descritivas de intervenções com impacto mensurável sobre doença grave.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Mapear quais parâmetros entomológicos de vetores florestais de P. knowlesi são realmente necessários para disparar alertas locais de prontidão clínica.

43057217.resumo: Zoonotic malaria challenges the assumption that interrupting human-to-human malaria transmission is sufficient to reduce the malaria burden. Plasmodium knowlesi, now the leading cause of malaria in Malaysia, shows how malaria can persist despite the elimination of indigenous human-only transmission. One Health has become the dominant response framework, but it provides limited guidance on how to allocate resources when evidence for many proposed interventions remains limited. We argue that zoonotic malaria activities should be prioritised according to the decisions they inform and their potential to reduce disease and death. Clinical readiness, including prompt recognition, referral and treatment of severe malaria, should remain the primary priority because it is the only intervention currently associated with improved clinical outcomes. Beyond clinical readiness, additional surveillance, ecological and wildlife activities should be judged by whether they trigger actionable responses rather than by alignment with the One Health framework.

43056343.titulo: Five-year trends in Malaria prevalence, Plasmodium species distribution, demographic patterns, and seasonal variation at Yejube health center, Baso Liben district, East Gojjam zone, Ethiopia, 2020-2024: Implications for Malaria elimination.
43056343.autores: Fenta A, Dilnessa T, … Abebaw D (7 autores)

resumo_blocos.racional: A compreensão das tendências temporais locais, da distribuição entre espécies de Plasmodium e dos picos sazonais é essencial para orientar estratégias de eliminação da malária em áreas endêmicas sujeitas a ressurgências.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Estudo retrospectivo institucional no Centro de Saúde de Yejube (distrito de Baso Liben, Etiópia) utilizando registros laboratoriais de microscopia entre janeiro de 2020 e dezembro de 2024. Dados de positividade, espécie parasitária, idade, sexo, ano e mês foram digitados no EpiData 4.2 e analisados no SPSS 24 por estatística descritiva, qui-quadrado e regressão logística binária multivariável (razões de chances ajustadas, AOR, com intervalo de confiança de 95% e p < 0,05).
resumo_blocos.resultados: Entre 7.806 lâminas examinadas, 1.066 foram positivas (13,65%). A positividade anual recuou de 20,08% em 2020 para 4,95% em 2023, mas ressurgiu para 14,66% em 2024; P. falciparum representou 49,6% dos casos, P. vivax 43,3% (predominando a partir de 2021) e infecções mistas 7,0%. Homens apresentaram maior positividade que mulheres (16,7% vs. 10,1%; AOR = 1,79; p < 0,001), com picos em outubro (21,5%) e novembro (20,3%) e mínimo em fevereiro (3,9%), além de maior chance em menores de 5 anos (AOR = 9,27), 15–29 anos (AOR = 8,39) e 30–59 anos (AOR = 9,60) frente a ≥60 anos.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Ilustra a transição epidemiológica para predomínio de P. vivax após quedas iniciais de P. falciparum e reforça a importância de vigilância entomológica e clínica contínua antes dos picos sazonais.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Cruzar a janela de transição de P. falciparum para P. vivax com dados de hipnozoítos e competência vetorial sazonal em regiões sob pressão de controle.

43056343.resumo:
Malaria remains a major global public health problem, with an estimated 282 million cases and 610,000 deaths in 2024, predominantly in the WHO African Region. Ethiopia continues to face substantial malaria transmission and has adopted an elimination strategy emphasizing surveillance, early diagnosis and treatment, and integrated vector control. Assessing local temporal, species-specific, demographic, and seasonal patterns is essential to guide targeted malaria elimination efforts.
To assess the five-year temporal trend of malaria prevalence, Plasmodium species distribution, demographic patterns, and seasonal variation among patients attending Yejube Health Center, Baso Liben District, East Gojjam Zone, Ethiopia.
A facility-based retrospective study was conducted in Yejube Health Center, Baso Liben District, East Gojjam Zone, Ethiopia, using laboratory records from January 2020 to December 2024. All individuals tested for malaria by microscopy during this period were included. Data on test results, Plasmodium species, age, sex, year, and month of diagnosis were extracted from laboratory logbooks. Data were entered in EpiData 4.2, then analyzed using SPSS 24. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and binary logistic regression were used to assess malaria test positivity and associated factors. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated, and statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.
A total of 7,806 blood films were examined from 2020 to 2024, of which 1,066 were positive for malaria, yielding an overall test positivity rate of 13.65% (95% CI: 12.91-14.44%). Annual positivity declined from 20.08% in 2020 to 4.95% in 2023, followed by a resurgence to 14.66% in 2024. Plasmodium falciparum accounted for 49.6% of confirmed cases, followed by P. vivax (43.3%) and mixed-species infections (7.0%). Although P. falciparum predominated in 2020, P. vivax predominated from 2021 onward. Malaria test positivity was significantly higher among males than females (16.7% vs. 10.1%; p < 0.001) and differed significantly across age groups (p < 0.001). Monthly positivity peaked in October (21.5%) and November (20.3%), with the lowest rate in February (3.9%). In multivariable logistic regression, males had higher odds of malaria positivity than females (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 1.79, 95% CI: 1.56-2.06). Compared with individuals aged ≥60 years, the odds were higher among children aged under five years (AOR = 9.27, 95% CI: 1.27-67.77), individuals aged 15-29 years (AOR = 8.39, 95% CI: 1.15-61.27), and those aged 30-59 years (AOR = 9.60, 95% CI: 1.31-70.25). Compared with August, the odds of malaria positivity were significantly higher in September, October, November, and May, but significantly lower in February.
Malaria test positivity at Yejube Health Center declined from 2020 to 2023 before resurging in 2024. Although P. falciparum predominated overall, P. vivax was the leading species from 2021 onward. Positivity was associated with sex, age, and month of diagnosis, with peaks in October and a secondary increase in May. These findings underscore the need for sustained surveillance and locally tailored malaria control strategies.
Strengthen malaria surveillance and seasonal preparedness, particularly before peak-positivity periods. Tailor prevention and health education to males and higher-risk age groups, and improve P. vivax diagnosis, treatment, and relapse prevention. Further studies incorporating population-based, meteorological, and entomological data are recommended to clarify transmission patterns and guide malaria control and elimination efforts.

43056729.titulo: Impact of Mass Testing, Treatment, and Tracking Interventions on the Genetic Diversity of Plasmodium falciparum in Two Endemic Ghanaian Communities.
43056729.autores: Asante A, Asa-Atiemo CKM, … Amoah LE (6 autores)
43056729.revista: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene

resumo_blocos.racional: Infecções assintomáticas por Plasmodium falciparum sustentam o reservatório de transmissão e desafiam metas de eliminação, mas ainda é pouco claro como campanhas repetidas de testagem, tratamento e rastreamento em massa (MTTT) modificam a diversidade genética e a multiplicidade de infecção (MOI) do parasito.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Foram selecionadas 566 amostras de sangue em papel-filtro (DBS) de indivíduos assintomáticos positivos para P. falciparum por PCR de transferência eletrônica fotoinduzida nas comunidades de Obom (n = 278) e Kofi Kwei (n = 288), em Gana, ao longo de três rodadas de MTTT em janeiro, maio e setembro de 2021. Após extração de DNA, realizou-se genotipagem de msp2 por PCR aninhada em gel para caracterizar as famílias alélicas 3D7 e FC27 e calcular a MOI.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A família alélica 3D7 predominou nos dois locais (71% em Obom e 68% em Kofi Kwei). Entre a primeira e a terceira rodada de MTTT, a MOI caiu significativamente em Obom (de 1,80 para 1,10; p < 0,0001) e em Kofi Kwei (de 1,60 para 1,30; p = 0,0007), sem variação significativa na distribuição alélica por faixa etária (3D7: p = 0,95; FC27: p = 0,59). 43056729.resumo: Asymptomatic malaria infections sustain transmission in endemic settings and may undermine elimination efforts. Mass testing, treatment, and tracking (MTTT) target both symptomatic and asymptomatic infections, but its impact on Plasmodium falciparum (P. falciparum) genetic diversity remains poorly understood. In the present study, temporal changes in P. falciparum merozoite surface protein 2 (msp2) genetic diversity and multiplicity of infection (MOI) were assessed during repeated MTTT interventions in two high-transmission Ghanaian communities. A total of 566 dried blood spot (DBS) samples, previously confirmed as P. falciparum-positive via photo-induced electron transfer polymerase chain reaction (PCR), were randomly selected from asymptomatic individuals in Obom (N = 278) and Kofi Kwei (N = 288) during three MTTT rounds conducted in January, May, and September 2021. Parasite DNA was extracted, and msp2 genotyping was performed using gel-based nested PCR to determine the 3D7 and FC27 allele diversity and MOI. The 3D7 allelic family predominated at both sites (Obom: 71%; Kofi Kwei: 68%). Multiplicity of infection declined significantly between the first and third MTTT rounds in Obom (1.80 to 1.10; P <0.0001) and Kofi Kwei (1.60 to 1.30; P = 0.0007). Despite reduced MOI, allelic diversity remained high, with 3D7 fragments ranging from ∼200 to 500 base pairs (bp) and FC27 fragments ranging from 300 to 500 bp. Allelic distributions did not differ significantly across age groups (3D7: P = 0.95; FC27: P = 0.59). A reduction in infection complexity was observed across the repeated MTTT intervention rounds, whereas parasite msp2 allelic diversity remained relatively high. These findings highlight the importance of integrating molecular surveillance into malaria control programs and targeting asymptomatic infections to reduce transmission reservoirs.

Após extração de DNA, realizou-se genotipagem de msp2 por PCR aninhada em gel para caracterizar as famílias alélicas 3D7 e FC27 e calcular a MOI.

43057277.titulo: Seasonal mass vaccination with R21/Matrix-M against malaria in The Gambia and Burkina Faso: an open-label, cluster-randomised, controlled trial.
43057277.autores: Dabira ED, Natama HM, … D'Alessandro U (25 autores)

resumo_blocos.racional: A vacina antimalárica R21/Matrix-M, recomendada pela OMS para crianças pequenas, poderia acelerar a eliminação se aplicada em vacinação sazonal em massa (SMV) a toda a população antes do pico de transmissão, exigindo validação controlada de segurança e efetividade em cenários de transmissão distinta.

Residentes com idade igual ou superior a 5 meses no braço intervenção receberam três doses mensais de 5 μg (<15 anos) ou 10 μg (≥15 anos) de R21 com 50 μg de Matrix-M entre maio e agosto de 2024, avaliando-se como desfecho primário a prevalência de infecção por Plasmodium falciparum por qPCR em inquérito transversal no pico de transmissão (novembro a dezembro de 2024).

43057277.resumo:
The R21/Matrix-M (R21) malaria vaccine candidate, recommended by WHO for use in young children, could be extended to the whole population. Seasonal mass vaccination (SMV) before peak malaria transmission could be a promising tool to accelerate progress towards malaria elimination. We aimed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of SMV with R21 in two malaria-endemic settings in west Africa.
This open-label, cluster-randomised, controlled trial was conducted in The Gambia, a setting with low-to-moderate seasonal transmission, and Burkina Faso, a setting with intense seasonal transmission. 54 medium-sized villages (30 in The Gambia and 24 in Burkina Faso) were randomly assigned (1:1) by use of computer-restricted randomisation to receive either SMV with R21 (intervention group) or no SMV (control group). All study villages received national standard malaria control interventions. In the intervention group, residents who were aged 5 months and older, willing to comply with trial procedures, and could provide written informed consent (from parents or guardians for children aged <18 years plus assent for children aged 12-17 years) were eligible for vaccination. The intervention was delivered as three monthly doses of 5 μg (participants aged <15 years) or 10 μg (participants aged ≥15 years) R21 plus 50 μg of Matrix-M. The primary outcome was malaria prevalence at peak transmission, defined as the proportion of participants with Plasmodium falciparum infection assessed by quantitative PCR. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06578572) and the Pan-African Clinical Trials Registry (PACTR202404544467702), and is ongoing.
The intervention was delivered between May 30, and Aug 21, 2024. A cross-sectional survey to estimate the primary endpoint was conducted between Nov 18 and Dec 6, 2024. The population available for vaccination varied across the three rounds. In The Gambia, among 4311 total residents in intervention villages, 2565 (59·5%) received three vaccine doses; in Burkina Faso, among 6235 total residents in intervention villages, 4072 (65·3%) received three vaccine doses. SMV with R21 reduced the odds of malaria infection by 70% (adjusted odds ratio 0·30 [95% CI 0·20-0·44]; p<0·0001) in The Gambia and by 25% (0·75 [95% CI 0·58-0·98]; p=0·036) in Burkina Faso. In The Gambia, prevalence decreased across all age groups, whereas in Burkina Faso the largest effect was observed in children younger than 5 years. The vaccine was safe and well tolerated. 651 adverse events were reported in 581 (13·5%) vaccine recipients in The Gambia, and 795 adverse events were reported in 705 (11·3%) vaccine recipients in Burkina Faso. Among 69 serious adverse events reported overall, only one was considered related to vaccination (febrile convulsions in a female participant aged 8 years after the second dose in The Gambia).
SMV with R21 reduced malaria prevalence in both settings. It could become an additional strategy for malaria control in endemic areas of seasonal transmission. In low-to-moderate transmission settings, the vaccine could accelerate progress towards elimination; in high-transmission areas it could further reduce the malaria burden.

43061578.resumo:
Aedes aegypti is a primary vector of several clinically significant arboviruses. This study aimed to develop a nanoemulsion-based co-delivery system incorporating permethrin and Eucalyptus globulus essential oil for mosquito repellent applications.
The essential oil composition of E. globulus was determined using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). Nanoemulsions were formulated using a low-energy spontaneous emulsification method and characterized for stability, droplet size distribution and zeta potential. The optimal formulation was further examined by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and evaluated for cytotoxicity. The repellent activity of eucalyptus essential oil, permethrin, their combinations, and the eucalyptus essential oil-permethrin nanoemulsion was assessed against female Ae. aegypti mosquitoes using the arm-in-cage assay.
The nanoemulsions exhibited a mean droplet size of 93.5 nm and a zeta potential of 60-70 mV, indicating good stability. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) confirmed the presence of spherical and uniformly dispersed droplets. The eucalyptus essential oil-permethrin nanoemulsion demonstrated strong repellency. A 3% permethrin concentration in the eucalyptus-permethrin nanoemulsion provided the maximum protection rate at 91.8%. In stability testing, the 1.5% version of the same nanoemulsion proved to be the most stable.
Eucalyptus globulus essential oil, especially in nanoemulsion form and combined with permethrin, shows promise as a natural repellent formulation against Ae. aegypti. However, field trials are essential to confirm these findings under natural conditions.

43057551.titulo: Semi-field efficacy of conspecific egg- and larva-derived chemical cues for manipulating Aedes aegypti oviposition.
43057551.autores: Mulatier M, Loïal A, … Vega-Rúa A (5 autores)

resumo_blocos.racional: Semioquímicos derivados de ovos e larvas coespecíficos modulam a escolha do sítio de oviposição de Aedes aegypti em laboratório, mas sua real eficácia comportamental em condições de semicampo permanece incerta para orientar armadilhas atrativas.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Em gaiolas externas de semicampo, ensaios de oviposição de dupla escolha avaliaram cinco compostos associados a ovos e larvas de Ae. aegypti — ácido (Z)-5-dodecenoico, ácido pentadecanoico, n-heneicosano, ácido palmitoleico e ácido dodecanoico — frente a infusão larval como controle positivo, além de testes com tela adesiva (sticky-screen) para distinguir atração espacial de estímulo por contato.
resumo_blocos.resultados: O ácido (Z)-5-dodecenoico mostrou tendência a elevar a oviposição (57% dos ovos; índice OAI = 0,14) e atração espacial significativa em tela adesiva sem contato (índice de atratividade = 0,45). Em contraste, n-heneicosano (OAI = -0,03) e ácido dodecanoico (OAI = -0,10) foram neutros, e os ácidos pentadecanoico e palmitoleico tenderam a leve dissuasão (OAI = -0,17 e -0,20), evidenciando discrepâncias marcantes entre ensaios laboratoriais e de semicampo.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Reforça a importância de validar sinais lipídicos e ácidos graxos mediadores de oviposição em condições próximas às reais e de separar atração olfativa de longo alcance do estímulo de postura por contato.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Avaliar se a composição de ácidos graxos na superfície de ovos de Aedes aegypti varia conforme a dieta materna (sangue controle vs. HFHS) e modifica a sinalização coespecífica.

43057551.resumo: Baited traps targeting gravid Aedes aegypti females are a promising tool for vector surveillance and control. Conspecific immature stages are known to influence oviposition-site selection and several egg and/or larvae derived compounds have been identified as potential oviposition cues under laboratory conditions. However, their performance under field conditions remains poorly understood, limiting their application in baited mass-trapping strategies. Using two-choice oviposition assays in outdoor cages, we evaluated under semi-field conditions the efficacy of five Ae. aegypti eggs and/or larvae associated compounds to influence oviposition in this mosquito species: (Z)-5-dodecenoic acid, pentadecanoic acid, n-heneicosane, palmitoleic acid and dodecanoic acid. An infusion of Ae. aegypti larvae was also tested under these conditions as positive control. We identified (Z)-5-dodecenoic acid as a potential volatile oviposition mediator, showing a trend toward increased oviposition (57 % of eggs received; oviposition attractivity index (OAI) = 0.14). For this compound, sticky-screen assays showed significant attraction compared to the control, excluding its detection by contact cues and suggesting its potential spatial activity to attract mosquitoes (attractivity index = 0.45). In contrast, n-heneicosane, and dodecanoic acid induced neutral oviposition responses (OAI = -0.03 and -0.1, respectively), whereas pentadecanoic and palmitoleic acids induced a trend toward slight oviposition deterrence in our settings (OAI = -0.17 and -0.20, respectively). Although previous laboratory or field evidence supporting their efficiency, our results reveal marked discrepancies between laboratory and semi-field behavioral responses. These findings emphasize the need for semi-field and field trials to assess mosquito semiochemicals, where long-range attraction can be distinguished from short-range oviposition stimulation, before considering their operational use in vector surveillance and control.

43058881.titulo: Bacterial and fungal diversity in Anopheles larval habitats with different productivities.
43058881.autores: Forson AO, Afrane YA, … Hurwitz I (7 autores)

resumo_blocos.racional: Comunidades microbianas de criadouros aquáticos influenciam oviposição, desenvolvimento e sobrevivência de larvas de Anopheles gambiae, mas a contribuição relativa de bactérias e fungos para distinguir habitats de alta e baixa produtividade larval ainda precisava ser caracterizada.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Criadores naturais de Anopheles no sul de Gana foram monitorados quinzenalmente por 6 meses e classificados em alta produtividade (larvas presentes em todas as visitas), baixa produtividade (presença intermitente) ou não produtivos (ausência constante). Amostras de água e larvas passaram por sequenciamento de amplicons bacterianos (16S rRNA) e fúngicos (ITS), com análise de diversidade beta (PERMANOVA) e análise discriminante linear.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A diversidade beta bacteriana diferiu significativamente entre criadouros produtivos e não produtivos (PERMANOVA, p = 0,006), ao passo que as comunidades fúngicas não mostraram separação global significativa. Como táxons indicadores de alta produtividade destacaram-se as bactérias Paraclostridium bifermentans e Bacillus spp. e os fungos Cladosporium halotolerans e Aspergillus penicillioides, enquanto Acinetobacter variabilis, Lactococcus garvieae, Candida tropicalis e Pichia kudriavzevii associaram-se a habitats de baixa produtividade.

resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Testar se a colonização larval por espécies de Bacillus associadas a alta produtividade modula a imunidade basal ou a susceptibilidade a larvicidas em criadouros controlados.

43058881.resumo:
Anopheles gambiae mosquitoes develop in diverse aquatic habitats, where microbial communities influence oviposition, larval growth, and survival. This study characterized bacterial and fungal communities across Anopheles larval habitats of differing productivity in southern Ghana.
Larval densities were monitored bi-weekly over 6 months. Water and larval samples were collected for bacterial (16S rRNA gene) and fungal (ITS) amplicon sequencing. Based on the consistency of Anopheles larval presence throughout the monitoring period, habitats were classified as high-productive (larvae present at every visit), low-productive (intermittent larval presence), or non-productive (larvae consistently absent).
The study revealed that distinct microbial signatures were associated with habitat productivity. Linear discriminant analysis identified Paraclostridium bifermentans and Bacillus spp. as indicator taxa for high-productive habitats, while Acinetobacter variabilis and Lactococcus garvieae were associated with low-productive habitats. For fungi, Cladosporium halotolerans and Aspergillus penicillioides were the primary discriminant taxa associated with high-productive habitats, while Candida tropicalis and Pichia kudriavzevii characterized low-productive habitats. Beta-diversity analyses revealed significant differences in bacterial communities between productive and non-productive habitats (PERMANOVA, p = 0.006), whereas fungal communities showed no significant separation.
These findings highlight an association between microbial assemblages and larval-habitat suitability and underscore the potential of microbiota-informed strategies to enhance vector surveillance and targeted larval control.

43061609.resumo:
Reliable mapping of malaria occurrence requires validation across environmentally distinct years and careful separation of model-derived probability from transmission intensity. This study developed a multi-sensor remote sensing and machine-learning framework for mapping annual malaria case occurrence in southeastern Iran.
Annual median composites of Soil Water Index (SWI), Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and Land Surface Temperature (LST) were generated from Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8/9 at 30m resolution. After quality control, 82, 168, 775 and 483 malaria case locations were retained for the Solar Hijri years 1400-1403 (2021-2025). Five spatially balanced pseudo-absence realizations were generated annually at a 1:1 ratio with a 300m exclusion buffer. Random Forest (RF) and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) were evaluated through complete four-fold leave-one-year-out validation with nested tuning. Performance, bootstrap confidence intervals, uncertainty, Getis-Ord Gi* clusters and SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) were assessed.
Across 20 outer evaluations, RF achieved ROC-AUC 0.685±0.045, PR-AUC 0.693±0.040, balanced accuracy 0.624±0.026 and Brier score 0.230±0.015. XGBoost achieved ROC-AUC 0.687±0.044, PR-AUC 0.691±0.043, balanced accuracy 0.625±0.033 and Brier score 0.231±0.015. Year-specific ROC-AUC ranged from 0.624 to 0.726. LST was the dominant predictor (48.27%), followed by NDVI (37.04%) and SWI (14.69%). Only 3.46-6.10% of pixels exceeded probability 0.70. Mean uncertainty was low (0.030-0.032) but spatially heterogeneous.
Both algorithms showed moderate, comparable performance with year-dependent variation. Maps provide relative probabilities for prioritizing field surveillance, not transmission estimates.

43059927.resumo: Prevention of West Nile virus (WNV) transmission relies heavily on vector surveillance and control. Current methods of population reduction are often reactive, guided by field surveillance. Vector control measures would benefit from neighborhood-scale, spatiotemporal predictions of WNV risk that could facilitate proactive, targeted surveillance to locations and times where vector and virus activity is expected to be highest. To determine the potential of predictions at this spatial scale, we approached model development in two phases: (1) inferential generalized additive models were developed using high-density mosquito data collected across Davis, CA that identified causal associations between neighborhood-scale spatial features and relative abundance or WNV infection prevalence in Culex tarsalis; (2) Bayesian predictive models for Cx. tarsalis abundance and WNV prevalence were constructed by incorporating neighborhood-scale spatial variables with temporal and climatic predictors, using historical vector surveillance data from Davis between 2006 - 2024. Inferential analyses revealed significant, time-dependent effects of nearby rice fields and distance from urban edge on Cx. tarsalis abundance and WNV prevalence. Final predictive models included terms for spatial, meteorologic, and temporal variables, and performed well for Cx. tarsalis abundance and WNV prevalence when challenged with novel data from Davis or the neighboring town of Woodland, CA. Results support the potential of neighborhood-scale models to predict WNV vector activity and inform vector control efforts, including routine operational control and placement of field trials.

43058754.resumo:
Despite wide-scale implementation of malaria prevention strategies, including seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC), a substantial disease burden persists. The R21/Matrix-M (R21/MM) malaria vaccine, recommended by the World Health Organization in 2023, is expected to substantially reduce this burden in children. However, the optimal delivery strategy in highly seasonal transmission settings remains uncertain. Integrating vaccine delivery with SMC campaigns may improve access, timeliness, and coverage, especially for the fourth dose. This trial will evaluate whether integrated delivery of R21/MM through SMC campaigns will provide non-inferior protection against malaria compared with routine Essential Program on Immunization (EPI)-based delivery or routine pre-seasonal delivery before SMC campaigns. Feasibility, acceptability, and cost-effectiveness will also be assessed.
This trial is a multi-site, phase IV, open-label, two-arm, cluster-randomized, non-inferiority trial conducted in the rural health districts of Boussé (Burkina Faso) and Dioila (Mali). Clusters, defined as peripheral health centers catchment areas, will be randomized separately within each country (1:1) and stratified by cluster size, with 20 clusters in Burkina Faso and 16 in Mali. Following written informed consent, trained study staff will enroll eligible children. Children aged 3-59 months living in intervention clusters and those aged 5-36 months living in control clusters will be eligible for vaccination. Children with previous malaria vaccination or conditions compromising participation will be excluded. Vaccination will be delivered through integrated SMC campaigns in the intervention arm and through year-round EPI-based delivery in Burkina Faso or pre-seasonal delivery before SMC campaigns followed by year-round EPI-based delivery in Mali. Power calculations will assume a non-inferiority margin of 0.10. The primary outcome will be the incidence of clinical malaria among children aged 5-36 months over 12 months after the first dose. Secondary outcomes will include adverse events following immunization, adverse events of special interest, serious adverse events, vaccine coverage, dropout rates, barriers and facilitators to implementation, stakeholder perceptions, and cost per disability-adjusted life year averted.
Beyond effectiveness and safety, the study will provide evidence to support integrated R21/MM delivery with SMC in highly seasonal transmission settings. The findings are expected to inform national and global malaria vaccine policies.

However, research conducted over the past decades has paid limited attention to ecological factors such as elevation, which is associated with the acquisition, transmission, and distribution of these parasites. In Colombia, knowledge of haemosporidian parasite diversity remains limited and fragmented. In this context, the aim of this study was to establish associations between haemosporidians and wild birds occurring at different elevations in the department of Caldas. Wild birds were captured and blood samples were collected at nine localities distributed across different elevations in four municipalities within the department. Haemosporidians were detected through microscopic examination of blood smears and molecular screening targeting the mitochondrial cytochrome b (cyt b) gene. In total, 74 samples from 45 bird species were analyzed, revealing an overall haemosporidian prevalence (Haemoproteus, Leucocytozoon, and Plasmodium) of 29.7% (n = 22). Infections were detected in 12 bird species, including residents (eleven individuals), neotropical migratory (two individuals), and introduced (nine individuals) birds. Fifteen parasite lineages were identified, including three lineages that are new to science (TURIGN01, TURFUS02, and ARRASS01). Finally, haemosporidian infections were detected across a broad elevational gradient (1021-2842 m a.s.l.), although prevalence varied considerably among localities. Furthermore, this study documents Leucocytozoon infection at 1021 m a.s.l., contributing to the growing evidence of the occurrence of this genus across a broad elevational gradient in Colombia.

However, it is unclear how Arizona public health and vector control professionals perceive the effectiveness of their current dissemination strategies. We conducted 18 key informant interviews with health department and vector control professionals across Arizona to evaluate current dissemination messaging, materials, and channels and to identify key gaps and challenges. Results indicated that messaging primarily focused on mosquito-borne disease prevention, emphasizing source reduction and personal protective behaviors, and the Fight the Bite campaign was frequently cited. Education on disease symptoms, care-seeking behaviors, and tick-specific risks and prevention practices was less commonly reported. Handouts and flyers were the most common materials, primarily available in English and Spanish. One-on-one interactions and social media were viewed as the most successful dissemination channels. Outreach typically occurred during the monsoon season and in response to positive human cases and vectors. Major challenges included limited funding, staffing constraints, and low public risk perception. Future dissemination should prioritize creating engaging, locally relevant content and adapting strategies to effectively reach the local community. County health departments should also expand education on locally relevant tick-borne diseases, such as Rocky Mountain spotted fever. These findings highlight barriers and opportunities to strengthen public health messaging and dissemination for vector-borne diseases within Arizona.

Using a subsample of 466 children from the 2013-14 Democratic Republic of the Congo Demographic and Health Survey, Doctor and colleagues concluded that the risk of missing infections through falciparum-specific RDT use was low, but that conclusion rested on only eight non-falciparum mono-infections. No nationally representative estimate exists for Uganda.
We analysed the 2024-25 Uganda Malaria Indicator Survey, in which children aged 6 to 59 months were tested by HRP2 based RDT and by real time PCR with species determination. We estimated survey-weighted prevalence of each species, alone and in mixed infection, and calculated RDT sensitivity separately for P. falciparum mono-infections, mixed infections containing P. falciparum, and non-falciparum mono-infections.
Among 6975 children, weighted parasite prevalence by PCR was 17.5% (95% confidence interval (CI) 15.6 to 19.4). Non-falciparum species were involved in 2.72% (95% CI 2.25 to 3.19) of children and were the sole species in 1.03% (95% CI 0.75 to 1.30). Weighted prevalence of mono-infection was 0.69% (95% CI 0.47 to 0.90) for P. malariae, 0.30% (95% CI 0.14 to 0.46) for P. ovale, and 4 of 6,975 children (exact 95% CI 0.016 to 0.147%) for P. vivax. RDT sensitivity was 82.3% (95% CI 80.0 to 84.6) for P. falciparum mono-infections and 90.7% (95% CI 84.6 to 95.0) for mixed infections containing P. falciparum, but only 14.3% (95% CI 7.1 to 24.7) for non-falciparum mono-infections. Of 267 PCR confirmed infections missed by the RDT, 60 (22.5%) were non-falciparum mono-infections.
Approximately one Ugandan child in a hundred carries a malaria infection that HRP2 based RDTs cannot detect, and such infections account for more than a fifth of all infections the RDT misses. Our estimates confirm, with nearly nine times as many events, the direction of previous findings from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, but they place the absolute burden in a national context that the earlier subsample could not support. This is a structural limitation of the diagnostic, not a failure of test quality, and it will not be resolved by improving HRP2 test performance.
