43056402.resumo: Mosquito-borne diseases (MBDs) remain a major global health challenge. Vector surveillance, pathogen detection, and clinical diagnosis are central to control efforts but are limited by labor-intensive workflows and shortages of trained personnel. Computer vision (CV) offers opportunities for scalable automation throughout the MBD management pipeline. We aimed to systematically characterize the applications of computer vision in mosquito-borne diseases research, summarize methodological developments, and identify opportunities and barriers to translating these advances into public health practice. We conducted a systematic review in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines, searching PubMed, Scopus, and IEEE Xplore for studies published between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2025, that applied computer vision to any aspect of MBD research or control. A total of 1,521 records were screened, and 650 studies met the inclusion criteria. Studies were categorized by computer vision application area, data types, algorithmic approaches, and data acquisition methods. Descriptive quantitative analysis and qualitative thematic synthesis were performed. The use of computer vision in MBD research increased significantly over the review period. Most studies focused on diagnostic applications, particularly Plasmodium detection in malaria microscopy. More recent work incorporated deep learning models for mosquito species classification, UAV- and satellite-based habitat mapping, and smartphone-based non-invasive diagnostic imaging. Emerging areas included 3D mosquito behavioral analysis and Internet of Things-enabled surveillance. We further developed a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive Mg2+ delivery system that specifically targets inflammation-damaged cells and significantly enhances fracture healing under inflammatory conditions. Collectively, our findings highlight the potential of Mg-based biomaterials in the treatment of inflammatory bone diseases.

43052374.resumo: The intestine adapts to environmental challenges by changing size, but whether such remodeling reflects fixed homeostatic restoration or context-dependent adaptation remains unclear. Here, using Drosophila melanogaster, we combine defined diets with oral bacterial infection to quantify midgut size, cell number, cell size, and epithelial turnover. We show that diet and infection reshape the midgut through distinct cellular programs. Infection causes rapid shrinkage only when the organ was initially large, whereas post-infection regrowth requires dietary nutrients and converges toward a diet-defined state rather than a fixed pre-injury size. Diet-driven expansion occurs primarily through enterocyte hypertrophy and persists after stem cell ablation, whereas infection-induced recovery requires intestinal stem cell/progenitor activity. Microbes also have context-dependent effects, acting as damaging stressors in nutrient-rich conditions but promoting growth and survival under nutrient-poor conditions. These findings reveal modular cellular strategies through which diet and microbes jointly shape epithelial plasticity.

43056288.resumo: Ribosome-associated quality control (RQC) ensures proteostasis by actively degrading aberrant translation intermediates on stalled ribosomes, yet its physiological role in gene regulation remains elusive. Here, we demonstrate that Drosophila circadian clocks employ RQC to sustain 24-h behavioral rhythms. RNA interference-mediated depletion of RQC components in circadian pacemaker neurons impaired free-running locomotor rhythms. In particular, the loss of Caliban (Clbn) function in clearing 60S-associated faulty polypeptides led to weak but long-period rhythms in adult locomotor activity. These behavioral phenotypes were accompanied by delayed accumulation of the core clock protein PERIOD (PER), most evidently in pigment-dispersing factor-expressing clock neurons, and dampened structural plasticity of their axons. per heterozygosity exaggerated CLBN depletion-induced period lengthening, whereas overexpression of the PER-associating factor TIMELESS blunted this effect. Clbn deficiency in Drosophila S2R+ cell cultures increased the generation of prematurely terminated PER species, particularly when PER translation is high, and sensitized full-length PER to phosphorylation-dependent decay. These findings support PER as a clock-relevant RQC substrate, providing a mechanistic link between translation flux, co-translational surveillance, and circadian timekeeping.

Here, we establish the transcriptional profile of the lymph gland, the Drosophila hematopoietic organ, and its associated niche, the posterior signaling center, at single-cell resolution and at different time points following an immune challenge. This molecular atlas of lymph gland cells at different time points after an immune challenge provides new insights into the control of stress hematopoiesis by discrete niche cell subsets.

Hypertriglyceridemia (HTG) is a prevalent dyslipidemia worldwide and an independent risk factor for cardiovascular disease and acute pancreatitis. ROC analysis demonstrated good diagnostic performance (AUC: 0.697, sensitivity: 86.40%, specificity: 45.00% at cut-off 0.873 ng/mL). In HFD-fed mice, serum ISG15 levels were significantly elevated, and immunohistochemistry and western blotting confirmed increased ISG15 expression in liver, subcutaneous white adipose tissue, and epididymal white adipose tissue.
ISG15 is independently associated with HTG and exhibits a nonlinear relationship with diagnostic potential. These findings establish ISG15 as a potential biomarker and suggest its involvement in the immunometabolic crosstalk underlying HTG pathogenesis, warranting further mechanistic investigation.

43059779.resumo: Most animal species exhibit some level of sociality. However, whether sociality-related traits evolved independently, or are instead derived from common core mechanisms, remains controversial. Nevertheless, an emerging theoretical framework stipulates that key aspects of how animals interact with their social environments may be regulated by a phylogenetically conserved genetic toolkit. Therefore, we hypothesized that mutations that lead to social deficits in specific human disorders may implicate genes that play conserved roles in the regulation of core social traits across Animalia. Specifically, here we focus on genes associated with Williams syndrome (WS), a rare human multi-system disorder characterized in part by hypersocial cognitive traits. WS is caused by a hemizygous chromosomal microdeletion of 25-28 protein-coding genes. Consequently, it has been hypothesized that haploinsufficiency in at least one of these genes plays an important role in the development and/or function of social neural circuits in humans. Because the Drosophila genome encodes orthologs of 17 of the 28 genes deleted in WS, we reasoned that at least some of them may serve a conserved role in the regulation of social traits across flies and humans, as predicted by the genetic toolkit framework. Using a neuron-specific RNAi knockdown screen, we identified eIF4H1 , an ortholog of a highly conserved subunit of the eukaryotic translation initiation complex eIF4F, as a candidate gene for neuronal regulation of sociality in the fly. We show that eIF4H1 expression is predominantly neuronal in the adult fly brain, and that its action plays a differential role in the organization of specific dopaminergic neuron subtypes that are associated with sociality and cognitive functions. These results indicate that eIF4H1 may serve a conserved function in regulating the development of the neuronal circuits that regulate social behaviors, thus supporting the idea of a conserved sociality genetic toolkit.

43060751.resumo: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) features chronic synovial inflammation and systemic immune disorders. Current treatments mainly rely on systemic immunosuppression, raising risks of infection and long-term immune injury. Local therapies reduce such risks but struggle to regulate systemic immunity. Emerging studies show the synovial immunometabolic microenvironment links local inflammation to systemic responses. Here, we developed a strategy based on chemically attenuated photosynthetic bacteria that couples lactate metabolism with photo-driven hydrogen production to achieve local metabolic reprogramming and systemic immune re-education. We screened a photosynthetic bacterial strain with high lactate metabolic capacity, which also exhibited enhanced hydrogen production. To ensure safety, bacteria were PEGylated to mask immunogenic moieties while preserving metabolic activity. Intra-articular injection disrupted pathological crosstalk and restored the Treg/Th17 balance locally. Circulating IL-6 levels decreased, restoring the systemic regulatory role of Tregs, thereby alleviating distant joint inflammation. These results demonstrate that local synovial metabolic reprogramming by engineered bacteria can induce systemic immune re-education, offering a conceptually new therapeutic strategy for treating autoimmune arthritis.

The uranium removal efficiencies were 72.7%, 58.5%, and 80.9% in the U1 (10 mg/L), U2 (50 mg/L), and U3 (100 mg/L) treatments, respectively. Antioxidant enzyme activities, including SOD, CAT and POD, together with GSH and GSSG contents, were altered under uranium exposure, indicating uranium-induced oxidative stress and antioxidant-related responses. FTIR and XPS analyses suggested that phosphate-, amide/carboxyl-, hydroxyl- and amino-related surface groups may participate in uranium association with the mycelial surface. Transcriptomic, proteomic and intracellular metabolomic analyses further revealed coordinated changes in carbon and energy metabolism, oxidative stress regulation, membrane transport-related proteins, phosphate metabolism-related proteins and intracellular organic acid-related metabolism. Notably, APase-related proteins may promote phosphate release and thereby facilitate phosphate-associated uranium immobilization, whereas ABC transporter-related proteins may contribute to membrane transport, efflux, and intracellular homeostasis under uranium stress. Overall, these candidate proteins suggest a mechanistic linkage between phosphate-mediated uranium immobilization and transporter-mediated uranium detoxification in A. niger, and provide prioritized molecular targets for future functional validation.

Importantly, FGF5 expression increased 1.35-fold, suggesting altered regulation of pathways associated with hair-follicle cycling.

43057756.resumo: Obesity is increasingly recognized as an immunometabolic disorder in which chronic low-grade inflammation is sustained by persistent upstream triggers rather than by adiposity alone. A central candidate trigger is intestinal barrier dysfunction with metabolic endotoxemia, defined as chronic, subclinical elevations of gut-derived microbial components, most notably lipopolysaccharide (LPS), in the absence of overt infection. In obesity, the intestinal barrier shifts toward increased functional permeability through coordinated remodeling of tight junction organization, mucus layer destabilization, and epithelial stress responses. This creates permissive conditions for microbial ligand passage while mucosal architecture can remain grossly intact. Importantly, systemic exposure is not determined solely by permeability, but by a coupled system involving luminal LPS availability, lipid-facilitated epithelial uptake and export, and context-dependent partitioning and clearance of LPS through binding proteins, lipoproteins, and hepatic handling. Low-dose, repeated LPS signaling engages innate immune pathways (including TLR4 and inflammasome-associated programs), amplifying cytokine production and stress kinase activity that impairs insulin signaling across metabolic tissues. The resulting organ crosstalk within the gut-liver-adipose axis helps explain heterogeneity in metabolic trajectories among individuals with comparable body mass index, particularly when visceral adiposity and postprandial lipid flux are considered. Therapeutic strategies that converge on this axis, including dietary fiber enrichment, microbiota-targeted interventions, metabolic pharmacotherapy, and bariatric procedures, provide proof of reversibility, yet human evidence remains limited by methodological heterogeneity and incomplete causal inference. Advancing the field will require standardized, dynamic barrier phenotyping, longitudinal designs, and stratified intervention trials to identify gut-driven subgroups and enable precision approaches to obesity-related cardiometabolic disease.

43052739.resumo:
The population density of rodents fluctuates due to intrinsic and extrinsic factors, inducing density-dependent effects on organisms and their habitats. The gut microbiota of herbivores plays a pivotal role in digestion, immunity, environmental adaptation, and host fitness. Crowding and host population density are considered among the driving factors that influence the gut microbiome of rodents. In laboratory settings, the gut microbiome of Brandt's voles exhibits distinct responses to density and crowding, which is a controlled environment and cannot mimic the natural system; however, its response in natural settings remains underexplored, which is more complex and shaped by biotic and abiotic interactions. Our study provides a comprehensive profiling of the (Lasiopodomys brandtii) gut microbiome at various population densities, under natural conditions, where diet and social structure fluctuate dynamically.
Across all densities, the dominant bacterial phyla were Firmicutes, Bacteroidota, Desulfobacterota, Campylobacterota, Actinobacteriota, and Patescibacteria. The Patescibacteria were significantly lower at medium (0.57% ± 0.117) and high densities (0.65% ± 0.423) than at low density (0.93% ± 0.339), whereas the Proteobacteria were higher at medium density (0.84% ± 0.518) than at low (0.43% ± 0.18) and high (0.54% ± 0.34) densities. Clostridia_vadinBB60 and F082 were reduced at high density relative to low and medium densities, and Lactobacillus abundance was lower at medium density compared with low and high densities. The microbial biomarkers at each density were (p < 0.05, LDA > 3): (Low; Bacilli, Helicobacter, Clostridiales_vadinBB60, F082, and Saccharimonadia), (Medium; Christensenellaceae), (High; Lactobacillus, Prevotella, and Lachnospiraceae). Alpha diversity was significantly lower at high density than at low and medium densities. At high density, Pielou's evenness, Shannon diversity index, observed richness, and Simpson's diversity were significantly lower than at low and medium densities (p < 0.05). Community structure differed significantly between low and high densities and between medium and high densities, but was similar between low and medium densities (p < 0.05). Bacterial predicted functional pathways varied significantly between low and medium densities and between high and medium densities, but showed no differences between low and high densities (p < 0.05). Density, AP, and pH were primary drivers of variance in microbial communities (p < 0.05). Mantel tests show that gut microbial diversity of voles is significantly correlated with density (r = 0.26, p = 0.0006) and water content (r = 0.19, p = 0.025), and microbial abundance is associated with soil water content (r = 0.26, p = 0.001) and aboveground biomass (AGB) (r = 0.24, p = 0.001). Density negatively affects microbial communities while positively affecting the soil physicochemical factors.
This study demonstrates that host population density serves as the primary driver of variation in gut microbiome in wild Brandt's voles. Soil properties and plant biomass act as secondary environmental filters. This work underscores the central role of host population dynamics in shaping the gut microbiome in natural systems, with potential implications for understanding how crowding stress influences host-microbe interactions in wild small mammals.

Analyses will account for the complex survey design and integrate epidemiological, environmental and social science data.
By combining nationally representative sampling with integrated human, animal, environmental and social science data, RACSMEI aims to generate comprehensive evidence on infectious disease exposure and transmission risks across diverse socio-ecological contexts in Cambodia. The study will provide policy-relevant insights to support One Health surveillance strategies and targeted public health interventions. The protocol was approved by the Cambodian National Ethics Committee for Health Research and the Institutional Review Board of Institut Pasteur Paris.

This study provides new insights into the metabolic basis of insect overwintering adaptation and the climatic adaptability of invasive forest pests.

43052273.resumo: Tissue injury is a pervasive feature of human disease, yet adult mammals exhibit limited regenerative capacity. A central determinant of regenerative outcomes is the inflammatory response, which orchestrates tissue repair through mechanisms that are evolutionarily conserved from Drosophila to mammals. Following injury, inflammation drives debris clearance, promotes the release of cytokines and growth factors, and contributes to the restoration of functional cells. However, dysregulated or unresolved inflammation can impair healing, drive scar formation, and ultimately result in organ dysfunction or failure. Here, we focus on recent advances in the spatiotemporal regulation of inflammation during tissue repair that have reshaped our understanding of its underlying mechanisms. We synthesize findings on the dynamic progression of repair from inflammatory initiation to active resolution and stem cell activation, highlighting features of immune cell plasticity and heterogeneity within injury-specific microenvironments, as well as the existence of pivotal macrophage-fibroblast interactions. Furthermore, we delineate the pleiotropic and context-dependent roles of key cytokines and signaling pathways in coordinating these processes. Finally, we discuss current and emerging therapeutic strategies, emphasizing the paradigm shift from broad immunosuppression toward precise modulation of inflammatory networks to promote regeneration and prevent fibrosis. Future progress hinges on integrating multiomic spatial atlases, precision immunomodulation, and standardized therapeutic protocols to decipher and manipulate immune-regenerative crosstalk, thereby driving the development of next-generation regenerative therapies.

43053502.resumo:
Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease initiated by dental plaque biofilm, characterized primarily by dysregulated host immune-inflammatory responses and progressive alveolar bone resorption, in which the dynamic M1/M2 polarization of macrophages serves as a pivotal regulatory factor. O-GlcNAcylation is a nutrient-sensitive post translational modification, and the relationship between O-GlcNAcylation and periodontitis needs further elucidation.
This article systematically reviews recent advances concerning the regulatory role of O-GlcNAcylation in macrophage-mediated periodontitis pathogenesis. Particular emphasis is placed on the bidirectional dose and site-specific effects of O-GlcNAcylation on macrophage polarization. In addition, the molecular mechanisms underlying pathological O-GlcNAcylation-mediated aggravated alveolar bone loss in diabetes-associated periodontitis are summarized.
Existing evidence identifies O-GlcNAcylation as a critical molecular hub linking metabolic derangements to periodontal osteoimmune destruction: it either potentiates M1-like pro-inflammatory responses and osteoclastogenesis, or facilitates M2-like reparative phenotypes and periodontal bone regeneration. In diabetes-associated periodontitis, aberrantly elevated O-GlcNAcylation significantly accelerates alveolar bone loss by enhancing inflammatory signaling and suppressing bone formation.
O-GlcNAcylation lays novel theoretical foundations and translational strategies for precision immuno-metabolic therapy of periodontitis, especially in patients complicated with metabolic syndrome.

ensaio.historia:
Durante quase um século, a parasitologia molecular operou sob um dogma redutor: para entender por que um mosquito transmite ou bloqueia a malária, ou por que o camundongo desenvolve edema cerebral, deveríamos buscar sempre "o gene" ou "a citocina". Mapeamos vias inteiras (Toll, Imd, JAK-STAT), sequenciamos transcriptomas de células únicas e quantificamos centenas de RNAs mensageiros.

No entanto, uma pergunta desconfortável permaneceu sem resposta na bancada: **como decisões vitais de infecção ocorrem em frações de segundo, muito antes de qualquer RNA polimerase conseguir transcrever um gene?**

Quando o oocineto atinge o microvilo do mosquito, a digestão do sangue está no auge. Milhões de eritrócitos se rompem, gerando uma pressão coloidosmótica massiva, liberação letal de hemo livre e fluxo turbulento não-newtoniano. O parasito não tem horas para esperar uma via gênica ser ativada. Ele precisa explorar as propriedades biofísicas nativas do epitélio: diferenças de potencial elétrico entre células vizinhas, zonas de menor tensão mecânica e condensação líquida de proteínas de superfície.

Se quisermos descobrir o que não sabemos que existe, precisamos sair da nossa própria vizinhança conceitual. É no cruzamento com a biologia de sistemas de organelas, com a bioeletricidade do desenvolvimento e com a física da matéria mole que residem as próximas grandes viradas da nossa bancada.

grandes_pesquisadores.conceito_chave: Contactoma Celular & Comunicação Não-Vesicular de Organelas
grandes_pesquisadores.historia:
Maya Schuldiner revolucionou a biologia celular ao quebrar o paradigma de que as organelas intracelulares se comunicavam exclusivamente através de vesículas secretoras (via clássica de Golgi e retículo).

Usando triagem robótica em larga escala de leveduras (SGA - Synthetic Genetic Array) combinada com microscopia de fluorescência de altíssima resolução, seu laboratório no Weizmann descobriu que organelas como retículo endoplasmático, mitocôndrias, peroxissomos, gotas lipídicas e vacúolos estão fisicamente conectadas por pontes proteicas especializadas ("tethers"), formando uma malha contínua chamada de 'contactoma'. Essas fendas de 10 a 30 nanômetros permitem o transporte ultrarrápido de lipídios, íons cálcio e intermediários metabólicos vitais, operando como cabos de alta velocidade dentro da célula.

grandes_pesquisadores.historia:
Michael Levin é pioneiro na redefinição da biologia do desenvolvimento e regeneração: enquanto a maioria dos biólogos encara eletricidade celular como algo restrito a neurônios e músculos, Levin provou que **todas as células vivas mantêm gradientes bioelétricos de membrana (Vmem)** e se comunicam através de junções comunicantes (gap junctions).

tecnicas_emergentes.tecnica: Espectroscopia AFM-IR em Nanoescala (Photo-Thermal Induced Resonance)
tecnicas_emergentes.o_que_e: Combinação de Microscopia de Força Atômica com Espectroscopia de Infravermelho (AFM-IR), permitindo caracterização química de espécies moleculares com resolução espacial de 10 a 20 nanômetros.
tecnicas_emergentes.historia:
Durante décadas, a espectroscopia de infravermelho clássica (FTIR) foi limitada pelo limite de difração da luz óptica (~2 a 10 micrômetros), sendo incapaz de identificar compostos químicos dentro de organelas isoladas.

O desenvolvimento do AFM-IR contornou esse limite físico ao utilizar a ponta ultrafina de um microscópio de força atômica para detectar a expansão térmica nanomecânica da amostra quando excitada por um laser infravermelho pulsado e sintonizável. Com isso, tornou-se possível obter o espectro de absorção química exato de nanodomínios lipídicos, agregados amiloides e depósitos minerais sem marcadores fluorescentes.
